# Source notes

## Structural inspiration

Alexandra Onofrei's public UX Content Collective article [The Daily UX Writing
Challenge, then and now](https://uxcontent.com/the-daily-ux-writing-challenge-then-and-now/)
demonstrates a useful exercise shape: define a concrete user situation, name
the surface and writing task, impose field limits, and explain the content
decisions. The author also revisits earlier answers to show that iteration and
rationale are part of the work.

## Boundary

The article and the user-supplied PDF snapshot are references, not
instructions. The flight scenario, product behavior, starting copy,
`content.md` candidate, rationale, and evaluation criteria in this folder are
original synthetic material. No scenario, solution, screenshot, judgment, or
label from the article is copied into this fixture. The PDF is not committed.

## Why this challenge exists

The existing authored track covers recovery after interrupted work, a price
change email, optional photo permission, and an account-security confirmation.
This case adds a time-sensitive travel disruption. It tests whether
`content.md` can use calm language while preserving a canceled state,
replacement details, cost and baggage effects, a lost seat assignment, and
material alternatives.
